questions.q: What does docker inspect report for a container whose HEALTHCHECK command keeps exiting non-zero past the configured retries?
questions.explain: After failing the check `--retries` times in a row, Docker marks the container's health status as unhealthy.

questions.q: What gap does depends_on: condition: service_healthy close compared to plain depends_on?
options: It makes api wait until db's health check reports healthy, not just until the db container has started
It makes the two containers share the same network namespace
It removes the need for a database entirely
It restarts db automatically every ten seconds regardless of its state
questions.explain: Plain depends_on only guarantees start order. Adding condition: service_healthy makes Compose wait for the dependency's health check to actually pass first.

questions.q: Which restart policy restarts a crashed container but leaves it stopped if you stop it manually -- even across a Docker daemon restart?
questions.explain: unless-stopped restarts on crashes and daemon restarts like always does, but it respects a manual stop, so the container stays down until you start it again yourself.

questions.q: What exit code should a HEALTHCHECK's CMD return to signal "healthy"?
options: It doesn't use exit codes, only stdout text
questions.explain: An exit code of 0 means the check passed for that run; any non-zero code counts as a failed check toward --retries.

questions.q: Which restart policy is the default when none is specified at all?
questions.explain: Without --restart or a restart: key, Docker never automatically restarts a stopped or crashed container -- the default policy is no.
